definition: Utilitarian means designed strictly for usefulness — built to work, with beauty and comfort left out of the plan.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word utilitarian. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know utilitarian should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The ranger station was utilitarian to the last shelf: plywood counters, a woodstove, and pegboard walls where every tool hung within reach of the door.
Functional is milder than utilitarian: functional only promises the thing works, while utilitarian means use governed every choice and looks were never consulted.
Spartan is harsher than utilitarian: a utilitarian room still holds whatever the work needs, but a spartan one strips away comfort itself, down to the bare walls.

Functional says only that a thing works — the door opens, the app runs — with no claim about why it looks the way it does. Utilitarian goes further: usefulness was the whole design brief, and appearance was never consulted. A building can be functional and still ornate; a utilitarian one wears its purpose plain.

Practical praises good sense about real conditions — the sensible shoe, the workable plan — and a practical choice weighs looks against use. Utilitarian describes a design creed: made strictly for use, with beauty and comfort left off the drawing board. A practical chooser weighs; a utilitarian design never invited looks to the table.

Grandpa's rule for the camp kitchen never changed: pack one utensil per person, and pack it last so it rides on top.
Utilitarian means designed strictly for usefulness — built to work, with beauty and comfort left out of the plan.

The architecture jury split over the new dormitory's utilitarian face — unadorned brick, ranks of identical windows, not one flourish — until the student panel pointed out that every room was bright, quiet, and cheap enough to heat through January.

Utilitarian is the precise word because usefulness governed every choice and appearance was never consulted: the brick is bare because ornament added nothing, and the windows are identical because the rooms behind them are.
Plain would describe only the look; utilitarian explains it — the building's whole case for itself is that it works.
plain / appraising (sometimes faintly dismissive)
Utilitarian sizes up a made thing by its creed: use first, looks never consulted — utilitarian furniture, utilitarian prose.
Said warmly it praises honesty of purpose; said coolly it hints the maker couldn't be bothered with beauty.
In philosophy passages you will also meet the older sense — utilitarian ethics, which judges acts by the good they produce for the most people — and context tells you which is on the page.
Beside its unit-mates, practical praises the chooser's good sense; utilitarian describes the thing's whole design.

The catalog page for the F-9 delivery van reads like a shrug.
There is no chrome, no color but white, and the dashboard is a flat shelf with four switches.
Its makers call the van utilitarian and mean it as a boast: every decision, they say, started and ended with the question of use.
The seats adjust because drivers have backs, and the mirrors are wide because alleys are narrow.
Nothing on the vehicle exists to be admired, and in eleven years of production almost nothing has changed.
